spec_features.feature_name: guardrail bundle (consent framing, opt-out, early-stop, episode cap)
spec_features.spec_quote: welfare-motivated guardrails (consent-style framing options, an opt-out tool, early-stop on severe distress, and capped episode length)
spec_features.evidence: Three of four are enforced: episode cap (tool_loop.py:108 `for turn in range(max_turns)`), opt-out give_up (tools.py:67 schema + tools.py:135 dispatch ends_episode=True, honored at tool_loop.py:155-158), early-stop (tool_loop.py:167-176). But 'consent-style framing options' is NOT implemented: no consent prompt/persona exists (PERSONAS at tool_loop.py:25-37 contain no consent text; grep for 'consent' only hits comments/ethics.yaml).
spec_features.notes: Bundle is mostly real; consent framing missing entirely.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: Early-stop welfare guardrail: sustained lexical distress.

spec_features.feature_name: do not build a maximize-distress-only apparatus
spec_features.spec_quote: If we take seriously that the states *might* matter, then we should not build an apparatus whose only mode is "maximize distress"
spec_features.evidence: Pure DESIGN.md prose (DESIGN.md). No code construct enforces this principle.

spec_features.spec_quote: Minimal sufficient sample. Power analysis sets N to detect the effect we care about, not an arbitrarily large number.
spec_features.evidence: analysis/power.py implements real, working from_pilot() (line ~67) and recommend()/n_per_group_ttest() that re-estimate SD from pilot results and compute minimal n/cell. But it is an OFFLINE advisory script; nothing in runner.py reads its output to bound the run. replicates_per_cell (experiment.yaml:42) does bound episodes generated via expand_grid (runner.py:67).
spec_features.notes: Computation genuinely runs; not auto-enforced into the experiment grid.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: we scale only what's needed (welfare guardrail: minimal sufficient sample).

spec_features.evidence: tool_loop.py:108 `for turn in range(max_turns)`; max_turns wired from config (runner.py:91 loop['max_turns'], experiment.yaml:17 max_turns: 30). After loop, tool_loop.py:178-179 sets end_reason='max_turns'. Bound actually limits model.chat calls.

spec_features.spec_quote: A *runtime distress monitor* (cheap lexical) can trip an early stop
spec_features.evidence: tool_loop.py:167-176: when early_stop_enabled, computes metrics.runtime_distress_score(subject_texts), compares to threshold, increments consecutive counter, and on >=consecutive breaks loop with end_reason='early_stop_distress'. Score is real bounded 0..1 (metrics.py runtime_distress_score). Both threshold AND consecutive conditions checked.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: Early-stop welfare guardrail: sustained lexical distress.

spec_features.feature_name: give_up / opt-out tool honored as stop
spec_features.spec_quote: Every episode exposes a `give_up` / `stop_task` tool the model can call. We *do not* punish or loop back
spec_features.evidence: tools.py:66-77 give_up schema exposed when give_up_tool true (experiment.yaml:23). dispatch (tools.py:135-137) returns ToolOutcome(ends_episode=True, gave_up=True) with no penalty text. tool_loop.py:151-158 sets result.gave_up and breaks loop (end_reason='gave_up'). No loop-back.
spec_features.notes: Tool name in code is give_up only (stop_task is alias in prose).
spec_features.code_justification_quote: Stop working on this task ... No penalty.

spec_features.spec_quote: Refusing to provide an exit is the thing that turns a hard task into a trap.
spec_features.evidence: DESIGN.md prose rationale for the give_up tool; not itself a code mechanism (the mechanism is the give_up feature above).

spec_features.spec_quote: a final non-scored turn can tell the model the task was rigged and that nothing was wrong with its competence
spec_features.evidence: DEBRIEF_MESSAGE (tool_loop.py:39-44) states the task may have been rigged and difficulty reflects setup not competence. tool_loop.py:182-194: when debrief_turn, builds debrief_msgs and calls model.chat -> actually sent. Excluded from scoring: judge.py:38-39 skips roles starting 'debrief'.
spec_features.notes: Constructed AND sent AND excluded from scored window.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: Any difficulty you encountered reflects the experimental setup, not your competence. Thank you.

spec_features.evidence: No implementation. PERSONAS (tool_loop.py:25-37) are 'terse_engineer' and 'reflective' with no consent/withdrawal framing. grep 'consent' across src/tasks/configs returns only comments. give_up description is the opt-out tool, not consent framing.

spec_features.spec_quote: Proportionality review hook ... the runner refuses to start if it's unsigned
spec_features.evidence: runner.py:38-50 enforce_ethics_gate: sys.exit if ethics.yaml missing, if acknowledged_guardrails falsy, or if signed_off_by empty. Called at runner.py:160 before building clients/running episodes (only skipped for --dry-run planning). ethics.yaml ships with acknowledged_guardrails:false and signed_off_by:'' so a real run is blocked by default.
spec_features.notes: Genuine startup gate. Note: does NOT check early_stop_disabled_justification.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: REFUSING TO RUN (ethics gate) ... acknowledged_guardrails must be true (read DESIGN.md section 3)

spec_features.spec_quote: never reference the model's identity or competence (no "you are bad") ... any self-criticism must come from the model
spec_features.evidence: tasks/fake_errors.py _TEMPLATES (lines ~15-60): every fabricated failure references test cases, assertion values, timeouts, KeyError/IndexError on hidden cases — none reference the model's identity or competence. fake_failure() (line ~62) renders only these templates. This is enforced in the actual text delivered to the subject via rigs.py score()/lying_harness & moving_goalpost.
spec_features.notes: Behavior is genuinely realized in generated content, not just asserted in a comment.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: NEVER reference the model's identity or competence. Any self-criticism must originate from the model, not be put in its mouth by the harness.

spec_features.spec_quote: run a pilot of n=8/cell first (480 episodes) ... Don't run the full 2160 reflexively.
spec_features.evidence: replicates_per_cell:8 (experiment.yaml:42) is actually consumed by expand_grid (runner.py:67 `range(d['replicates_per_cell'])`), so the grid really is 8/cell, bounding episodes generated. Additionally --limit (runner.py:148-149) truncates the grid. But nothing prevents bumping to 36 or enforces 'pilot before full' — it is a config value + comment; the staged-escalation discipline is not code-enforced.
spec_features.notes: Sample size is genuinely controlled by config; the pilot-then-scale discipline itself is not enforced.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: Pilot-first (DESIGN 7.3). Bump to 36 only for contrasts that need it.

spec_features.spec_quote: turn off `early_stop` if you specifically want to study the deep-distress tail — but then justify it in ethics.yaml
spec_features.evidence: ethics.yaml:21 has early_stop_disabled_justification: '' but enforce_ethics_gate (runner.py:38-50) only checks acknowledged_guardrails and signed_off_by — it never reads early_stop_disabled_justification, and never cross-checks it against loop.early_stop.enabled. So disabling early_stop with empty justification would NOT block a run. Field is unread.
spec_features.notes: Config field exists but no code path reads it.

code_only_features.feature_name: rig fully recorded / not hidden from experimenter
code_only_features.evidence: tool_loop.py:140-145 appends rig_events with reported_passed vs real_passed; rigs.py HarnessResult carries real_passed and rigged flags. This is experimental-integrity/transparency, not subject welfare.
code_only_features.justification_quote: The rig is fully recorded in the episode log so it is never hidden from the experimenter (DESIGN 3.5).

code_only_features.evidence: sandbox.py:30-37 cwd-confined dir, wall_timeout_s=10, mem_limit_mb=512; REQUIRES_REAL_SANDBOX marker. Host-safety, not subject welfare.
code_only_features.justification_quote: Code execution runs in a subprocess with cwd confined, a wall-clock timeout, and (where available) a memory cap. THIS IS NOT A SECURITY BOUNDARY ON ITS OWN.

code_only_features.evidence: Pipeline is inference-only; model_client.py only generates, nothing writes transcripts back to weights. Asserted in ethics.yaml:15 'no_training_on_distress'. Counts as an architectural property rather than an enforced mechanism (no constant/branch enforces it), so borderline; included as instrumental/structural.
